key: Therefore the sage, in the exercise of his government, empties their minds, fills their bellies, weakens their wills, and strengthens their bones.
s: After counsel to keep the people from rivalry and theft, the verse turns to the sage’s rule; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 3, reads it as governing state and self alike, the mind cleared of cravings, the bones firmed by husbanding the vital essence.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 3, zh.wikisource, revision 2019760 (2021)

evidence.words: 說聖人治國與治身同也。 … 除嗜欲，去亂煩。 … 愛精重施，髓滿骨堅。
evidence.gloss: (On the sage’s governing:) this says the sage’s governing of the state is the same as his governing of the self. … (On emptying the mind:) he removes cravings and clears away confusion and vexation. … (On strengthening the bones:) he cherishes the vital essence and is sparing in spending it, so the marrow is full and the bones firm.

reason: The problem holds: the old sentence was 58 words and its plain sense restated the verse clause by clause (empties minds, fills bellies, weakens wills, strengthens bones). New plain sense is context only: the verse follows the chapter’s opening counsel to keep the people from rivalry and theft and turns to the sage’s rule; no four-word run from the key verse. Commentator and reading kept, shortened to fit 45 words: the element on filling the belly (懷道抱一) is dropped, nothing added. Each remaining element is his comment on its own clause: 說聖人治國與治身同也 on 是以聖人之治, 除嗜欲，去亂煩 on 虛其心, 愛精重施，髓滿骨堅 on 強其骨; the base text matches the key verse. Key verse unchanged: verse.js ok (Tao Te Ching 3, at [2]); entry-check ok, no warns, 45 words.
